heros.infro: King François of France commanded navigator Jacques Cartier to find a Northwest Passage to China and gold in the New World. On his second voyage in 1535-36, he discovered the Saint Lawrence River and named the region Canada. He befriended the Iroquois and renamed one of their settlements Mont Royal, which later became Montreal. The area was to become the center of French power in the New World and the hub of further French exploration of Canada and the Mississippi River Basin.
heros.name: Jacques Cartier

heros.infro: Considered to be the first great philosophers in the field of scholastic philosophy, Boethius is considered among the greatest of Western thinkers.
heros.name: Boethius

heros.infro: Mestwin II was a Duke of Pomerelia from 1266 until 1294. He united all the lands of Pomerelia and became the sole ruler of all of Pomerelia by kicking out all of his brothers from his lands. Mestwin concluded the Treaty of Kępno in 1282, which made Duke Przemysł II his successor in all his possessions. The resulting tensions between Brandenburg and Poland led to the Teutonic takeover of Danzig in 1308.
heros.name: Mestwin II, Duke of Pomerania

heros.infro: Heinrich Walpot von Bassenheim, also known as Henry Walpot, was the first Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights, serving from 1198 to 1200. Walpot came from a wealthy family from Mainz. He was in favor of turning the Teutonic Knights organization into a military order. In 1199 he received a copy of monastery rules from Gilbert Horal, the Grand Master of the Knights Templars, on behalf of Pope Innocent III. It was based on the rules of the Templars. Walpot died and was buried in Acre.
heros.name: Heinrich Walpot von Bassenheim

heros.infro: A true master of many disciplines, bacon was successful as a politician, a philosopher and a scientist.  His greatest contribution to Western culture was the popularization of the scientific method.
heros.name: Francis Bacon

heros.infro: Christopher I was King of Denmark between 1252 and 1259. He was selected King after the untimely death of his older brother Abel in the summer of 1252. Christopher spent most of his rule fighting off his many opponents. The King died "unexpectedly" after taking Holy Communion. According to newly discovered sources King Christopher died after drinking poisoned communion wine given to him by Abbot Arnfast of Ryd Abbey in revenge for the king's oppression of the church.
heros.name: Christopher I of Denmark
